newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican opposition to revise economic policy-paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexican opposition to revise economic policy-paper.

text.p: Mexico's conservative National Action Party (PAN) plans to discuss and revise the country's future economic policies in the lower house of congress, the daily Reforma reported on Friday.

Reforma cited PAN leader Felipe Calderon as warning President Ernesto Zedillo not to try to impose his government's economic plans on congress given the fact that his ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) no longer had an absolute majority.
"Economic policy will be up for discussion and revision," Calderon was reported as saying.

In key mid-term elections held July 6, the PRI lost part of its seven decades grip on power when it failed to hold onto its absolute majority in the lower house of congress that approves the government's budget proposals.
The PRI's control of congress meant that legislators traditionally rubber-stamped executive proposals and government budgets.
"A lower house of congress in which his (the president's) party does not have an (absolute) majority means that economic policy will be up for discussion and revision ..." Calderon said.
Zedillo has repeatedly said he would not cave in to pressures from other political parties or groups to change his government's economic policy.

Pressure has been mounting on Zedillo's government to modify certain economic cornerstones of its economic policy. Lowering Mexico's IVA, equivalent to Value Added Tax (VAT), has been one topic at the center of debate.
Calderon reiterated that his party will propose a reduction in IVA in gradual steps, Reforma said.
Manuel Lopez Obrador, leader of the left-leaning Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), also said Zedillo should not try to impose his personal economic projects, Reforma added.

"We do not agree with the president, we think that economic policy must be revised and the best place to do that is in the lower house of congress where we must agree a budget that attends to the needs of the majority of Mexicans," Lopez Obrador said.
The government normally sends budget proposals to congress for the upcoming year in the final quarter of the year.
